name: StudioMeta – AI Receptionist and WooCommerce Assistant
author: stdmeta

sections.description:
StudioMeta turns your WordPress site into a 24/7 AI receptionist — a real-time AI voice agent and AI chat widget that answers visitors by voice or text, books real appointments on your calendar, and, on a WooCommerce store, answers “where is my order?” and product questions from your own live data. It only hands off to a human when it should.

Unlike a scripted chatbot, StudioMeta reads your own site content, docs and pages to build its knowledge base automatically — so it answers from what you’ve actually published, not a canned script.

Every install includes a free trial — no signup, no credit card required. Click “Start Free Trial” to get 30 voice minutes and 100 chat messages, for 30 days.

Why an AI voice agent, not just another chat widget?

  • Answers by real-time voice, not just text — visitors talk to it like a phone call, right in the browser
  • Books real appointments — checks your working hours and books open calendar slots on the spot, no calendar tool or webhook required
  • Trained on your own content — point it at your site, docs or PDFs and it builds a knowledge base in one click
  • No API key to manage — the AI runs on our hosted infrastructure
  • No coding required — install, click Start Free Trial, and the widget is live
  • Try before you buy — 30 voice minutes and 100 chat messages for 30 days, no credit card

Key features

  • AI voice agent — visitors talk to your AI agent, the agent talks back (real-time, streaming) — like a phone call to your front desk
  • AI live chat — the same agent in a classic chat widget, for visitors who prefer typing
  • Appointment booking — checks your working hours and books real calendar slots during the conversation
  • Google Calendar sync — connect in one click, no API key; busy times stay off what visitors are offered
  • Multi-language — English, Persian (فارسی), Arabic, French, Spanish, and more, auto-detected per visitor
  • Knowledge base import — auto-crawl your site to train the agent on your content
  • Customizable widget — color, position (bottom-left/right), style (FAB or pill), six ready themes
  • Gutenberg block — drag a “Voice AI Widget” block into any page or post to place the widget inline, no shortcode needed
  • Suggested questions — chips that prompt visitors with common questions
  • Agent customization — name, voice, response style, system prompt, timezone
  • WooCommerce store assistant — answers order and product questions from your own store: order status for guest checkouts as well as account holders, live prices, stock, specifications, and a one-click link that fills the cart and opens checkout
  • Answers your phone too — connect your own Twilio number and the same agent answers real phone calls
  • Smart Navigation — opens the page a visitor asks for, such as pricing or contact, mid-conversation
  • Live chat with your team — visitors who ask for a person reach your team via Telegram, on your site
  • CRM integration — connect your own HubSpot account and every call and chat logs as a contact with notes
  • Custom tools & automation — connect your agent to any automation platform (n8n, Make, Zapier) via a webhook you provide
  • Usage dashboard — see voice minutes used, sessions, and remaining quota
  • Smart fallback — when one quota is exhausted, the other stays available

Built for

  • Healthcare & dental clinics — books appointments, screens intake questions
  • Real estate agencies — qualifies leads, schedules showings
  • Law firms — takes after-hours intake through the site
  • Restaurants — handles reservations and hours questions
  • Ecommerce stores — answers “where is my order” and product questions straight from WooCommerce
  • Any small business that doesn’t want to miss another website inquiry

How the trial works

  1. Activate the plugin, then click Start Free Trial in the admin panel
  2. Use 30 voice minutes and 100 chat messages on real visitor conversations, within 30 days
  3. When the voice quota is exhausted, the chat widget keeps working (and vice versa)
  4. When both are exhausted, the widget shows an upgrade button linking to our pricing page

Upgrading to a paid plan

If you want unlimited or higher quotas, visit studiometa.io/pricing. After purchase, your widget reactivates automatically within 5 minutes — no need to copy and paste a license key.

External services

This plugin connects to external services provided by StudioMeta to function. This is required because the plugin is an interface to a hosted AI assistant. The following services are used:

1. StudioMeta Voice AI API (api2.studiometa.io)

What it does: Hosts the AI agent. Handles license validation, quota tracking, knowledge base storage, agent configuration, voice/chat session orchestration, and dashboard analytics.

When it is contacted:

  • On plugin activation: to issue a free trial license (sends site URL, admin email, business name, site fingerprint, WordPress version, plugin version, language preference)
  • When you save settings or agent configuration: to sync your changes to the hosted agent
  • When you click “Import KB from Website”: to crawl your public pages and build a knowledge base
  • When you click “Optimize with AI”: to improve your system prompt
  • When the admin Dashboard loads: to fetch usage statistics
  • Every 5 minutes (cached): to check current quota status (decides whether the widget shows voice, chat, both, or an upgrade button)
  • When a visitor uses the voice or chat widget: a WebSocket connection is opened to wss://api2.studiometa.io/voice to stream audio and messages

Data sent: site URL, admin email, business name, business phone number (only if you enter one), your custom agent configuration (name, voice, system prompt, knowledge base text, suggested questions, custom tools), and during sessions: visitor audio and chat messages.

What is kept, and for how long: a written transcript of each voice conversation (both what the visitor said and what the agent replied) is stored on our servers and deleted automatically 90 days after the call. Call audio is kept only if you turn on Save call audio under Voice AI → Widget → Privacy. It is off by default; when it is on, recordings are stored so that you can play them back under Voice AI → Voice Summary, and are deleted automatically 30 days after the call. The short AI summary of a call is kept after that, so the Voice Summary screen still shows what older sessions were about once the word-for-word text is gone; summaries are removed when your account is deleted, or sooner on request. Because conversations are transcribed — and recorded, if you turn that on — you should say so on your site; some jurisdictions require everyone in a conversation to be told before recording begins.

If you enable the WooCommerce Store Assistant: when a visitor asks about a product or an order during a conversation, the agent requests that record from your own site and the answer passes through api2.studiometa.io so it can be spoken or written back. That means the product details, or the status, items and total of the order the visitor asked about, are sent for the duration of that reply. Nothing is copied to us in advance: your catalog and orders are read live from your site at the moment of the question, and only the record asked about is involved. The feature is off until you turn it on under Voice AI → Integrations.

Data NOT sent: WordPress user accounts or passwords, post content (unless you explicitly import it via “Import KB”), visitor IP addresses.

  • Service homepage: https://studiometa.io
  • Terms of Service: https://studiometa.io/terms/
  • Privacy Policy: https://studiometa.io/privacy-policy-2/

2. StudioMeta Workflow Webhooks (n8n.studiometa.io)

What it does: Sends transactional emails (welcome email on activation, license key email after purchase, usage alerts at 80% and 100%, monthly usage report).

When it is contacted:

  • Once on plugin activation: to trigger the welcome email
  • When usage thresholds are crossed (server-side): to trigger usage alert emails

Data sent: admin email, site URL, business name, current plan, usage percentages.

  • Service homepage: https://studiometa.io
  • Terms of Service: https://studiometa.io/terms/
  • Privacy Policy: https://studiometa.io/privacy-policy-2/

3. HubSpot (api.hubapi.com) — optional, only if you connect it

What it does: Syncs leads captured by the voice/chat widget (name, email, phone, notes) into your own HubSpot CRM as contacts.

When it is contacted: Only if you explicitly connect HubSpot under Voice AI → Integrations by entering your own HubSpot Private App Token. If you never connect it, the plugin never contacts HubSpot.

  • When you click “Connect”: one test request to api.hubapi.com to verify your token
  • When the widget captures a lead: the lead’s name, email, phone, and notes are sent to api.hubapi.com to create/update a contact in your HubSpot account

Data sent: your HubSpot Private App Token (stored in your WordPress database, sent only to HubSpot), and captured lead fields (name, email, phone, notes).

  • Service homepage: https://www.hubspot.com
  • Terms of Service: https://legal.hubspot.com/terms-of-service
  • Privacy Policy: https://legal.hubspot.com/privacy-policy

4. Google Gemini Live (indirectly, via api2.studiometa.io)

The AI capabilities are powered by Google’s Gemini Live API. The plugin does not contact Google directly — all requests go through api2.studiometa.io, which forwards them to Google. You do not need a Google account or API key.

  • Google Gemini Terms: https://ai.google.dev/terms
  • Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

5. OpenAI Realtime (indirectly, via api2.studiometa.io)

On the Premium and Enterprise plans, voice conversations are powered by OpenAI’s Realtime API instead. The plugin does not contact OpenAI directly — all requests go through api2.studiometa.io, which forwards them to OpenAI. You do not need an OpenAI account or API key. Plans other than Premium and Enterprise do not use this service.

Data sent: the visitor’s microphone audio and typed messages during a voice conversation, plus your configured agent name, greeting, system prompt and knowledge base.

  • OpenAI Terms of Use: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use
  • OpenAI Privacy Policy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy

6. Google Calendar (calendar.googleapis.com) — optional, only if you connect it

What it does: Lets the AI agent book real appointments during a conversation. Reads busy times from your connected Google Calendar so the agent never offers a slot you’re already booked, and creates a calendar event when a visitor books.

When it is contacted: Only if you explicitly connect Google Calendar under Voice AI → Appointments by clicking “Connect Google Calendar” and signing in through Google’s own consent screen. If you never connect it, the plugin never contacts Google Calendar, and appointment booking still works from the working hours you set — it simply won’t check your calendar for conflicts.

  • When you connect: a one-time OAuth sign-in with Google, requesting only free/busy visibility and the ability to create/edit events it creates — never your full calendar or any other Google data
  • When a visitor asks about availability: your calendar’s busy times are checked (cached briefly) to avoid offering a taken slot
  • When a visitor books: an event is created on your calendar with the appointment details

Data sent: an encrypted access credential (stored on StudioMeta’s servers, never in your WordPress database), and appointment details (visitor name, email, and time) when creating a calendar event.

Data NOT sent: the content of your other calendar events, contacts, or any other Google account data.

You can disconnect at any time from Voice AI → Appointments, or by revoking access directly from your Google Account permissions page.

  • Google Calendar Terms: https://developers.google.com/terms
  • Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

7. Twilio (api.twilio.com) — optional, only if you connect it

What it does: Lets real phone calls to a phone number you own be answered by your AI agent, using your own Twilio account. You keep your own Twilio account, buy your own number, and pay Twilio directly for call minutes and number rental — StudioMeta does not resell or bill you for Twilio usage. Talk time on answered calls counts against the same monthly voice minutes as the website widget.

When it is contacted: Only if you explicitly connect a Twilio account under Voice AI → Integrations by entering your Twilio Account SID, Auth Token, and phone number. If you never connect it, the plugin never contacts Twilio.

  • When you connect: your Account SID and Auth Token are verified once against Twilio to confirm they are valid before being saved
  • When someone calls your connected number: Twilio sends the call to StudioMeta’s servers, and the caller’s audio and the agent’s replies are streamed for the duration of the call

Data sent: your Twilio Account SID and Auth Token (stored encrypted on StudioMeta’s servers, never in your WordPress database), the phone number you connected, and during calls: the caller’s audio. Phone calls are transcribed on our servers exactly as widget calls are, and recorded only if you turn on Save call audio, with the same 30-day retention for the audio.

Data NOT sent: your Twilio billing details, SMS messages, call recordings held in your Twilio account, or any other data from your Twilio account.

You can disconnect at any time from Voice AI → Integrations, or by removing the webhook from your number in the Twilio Console.

  • Twilio Terms of Service: https://www.twilio.com/legal/tos
  • Twilio Privacy Policy: https://www.twilio.com/legal/privacy

8. Telegram (indirectly, via api2.studiometa.io) — optional, only if you connect a group

Lets your team take over a chat from your own Telegram group, connected under Voice AI → Staff Requests. The plugin never contacts Telegram itself; StudioMeta’s servers relay messages. When a chat visitor asks for a person, the group receives their request, the contact details they gave and the conversation so far, then the messages exchanged while a team member chats with them. Those messages stay in your group, under Telegram’s terms, until you delete them. Without a connected group nothing is sent to Telegram.

  • Telegram Terms of Service: https://telegram.org/tos
  • Telegram Privacy Policy: https://telegram.org/privacy

How to opt out

If you do not want the plugin to contact these services, simply deactivate and uninstall the plugin. The plugin cannot function without the hosted services because the AI assistant runs on our infrastructure (similar to how an Akismet plugin needs the Akismet service, or a Mailchimp plugin needs Mailchimp).

Third-Party Assets

Vazirmatn v33.003 by Saber Rastikerdar, used for Persian and Arabic text.
Licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (see assets/fonts/OFL.txt) and
distributed unmodified. Only the Non-Latin subset is bundled, and it is served
from this plugin folder — no font CDN is contacted, so no visitor or
administrator IP address is sent to a third party.
Source: https://github.com/rastikerdar/vazirmatn
sections.installation:
1. Upload the studiometa-voice-ai folder to /wp-content/plugins/, OR install through the WordPress plugin browser
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress
  3. Click Start Free Trial in the admin notice to activate your free trial — you’ll see the Voice AI menu item in your WordPress admin sidebar
  4. Click Voice AI → My Agent to customize your assistant’s name, voice, and knowledge base
  5. The widget appears as a floating button on every page of your site — or place it inline with the Voice AI Widget block in the block editor, or the shortcode [smva_widget]
sections.faq:
Do I need to create an account?

No. Click Start Free Trial in the admin panel after activation. No account or credit card needed.

Is StudioMeta Voice AI free?

Every install starts with a free trial (30 voice minutes + 100 chat messages for 30 days, no credit card). During the trial, if one quota runs out the other keeps working. When both run out or the 30 days end, upgrade to keep going.

Do I need coding skills to set this up?

No. Install the plugin, click Start Free Trial, and the widget appears automatically. Customizing your agent’s name, voice, and knowledge base is done through simple admin screens — no code, no API keys.

Will this slow down my site?

The widget script loads in the footer after your page content, so it doesn’t block your site from rendering.

Which AI powers the assistant, and do I need my own API key?

The assistant runs entirely on StudioMeta’s hosted AI Engine. You don’t need your own API key or a separate AI subscription — everything is included in the plugin.

What happens when my trial runs out?

The widget shows an upgrade button linking to our pricing page. If you’ve used all your voice minutes but still have chat messages, the widget shows only the chat tab (and vice versa).

Will the widget reactivate automatically after I purchase?

Yes. Within 5 minutes of your purchase, the plugin detects the upgrade and the widget switches back to full mode. You don’t need to copy and paste a license key.

Can I customize the voice and personality of the agent?

Yes. Go to Voice AI → My Agent to set the agent’s name, voice (multiple voices available), response style (concise / balanced / detailed), system prompt, and knowledge base.

What languages does the assistant speak?

English, Persian (فارسی), Arabic, French, Spanish, and more. Set the language under Voice AI → General.

Can I add the widget to specific pages only?

Yes. By default the widget appears site-wide. You can disable that and use the shortcode [smva_widget], or the Voice AI Widget Gutenberg block, to place it manually on selected pages.

Is there a Gutenberg block?

Yes. Search for “Voice AI Widget” in the block inserter and drag it into any page or post to place the widget at that exact spot — no shortcode needed. It works the same as the [smva_widget] shortcode.

Does this work on mobile?

Yes. The widget is fully responsive and supports voice on mobile browsers that allow microphone access (most modern browsers do).

Can a visitor talk to a real person?

Yes, in text chat, if you connect your team’s Telegram group under Voice AI → Staff Requests. When a visitor asks for a person, the group gets their request and the conversation so far; whoever taps “I’ll take it” chats with them from Telegram while they stay on your site. If nobody takes it within the wait you set, the request is saved for later and the visitor is told so, with a reference.

Do my team members need to install anything?

Only Telegram, on their phone or computer. Create a group with the people who should answer visitors, then click “Connect a Telegram group” in the plugin and pick that group. Sending /help in the group shows how to take, answer and end a chat.

What happens when the assistant cannot decide something?

With Staff Requests turned on, a request that needs a person — an exception, a price you have not given the assistant — is recorded for your team instead of being answered, and the visitor is told exactly what you wrote they should expect. Visitors can later ask where it stands, giving its reference and the email or phone they used.

Does the plugin send data anywhere?

Yes. Because the AI runs on our hosted infrastructure (api2.studiometa.io), the plugin sends configuration data and conversation contents to our servers. See the External Services section above for full details.

Is uninstalling the plugin clean?

Yes. When you uninstall, the plugin removes all its options, transients, and licensing data from your WordPress database.

Where can I get support?

Visit studiometa.io/contact or use the support forum on this plugin’s WordPress.org page.
sections.changelog:
1.11.0

  • New: guided setup. A new site is walked through seven steps: business type, learning from your website, where you are, voice, booking, call audio, and a live test of the chat on your own site. Each step is saved as you go, and you can reopen it from the dashboard.
  • Your time zone is detected from your browser, so appointments and reminders run on your clock instead of UTC.
  • Law firm, real estate and gym agents now follow fixed rules your own instructions cannot remove, and “Optimize with AI” keeps every sentence about what your agent must not do or promise.
  • Train My Agent no longer stops when only the suggested questions fail.

1.10.1

  • New: choose your business type (dental, medical, veterinary, restaurant, salon, home services, law firm, real estate, online store, auto repair, gym or general) and review suggested questions, quick-action buttons, appointment length and a starter prompt before anything changes. Anything you set yourself is left alone unless you tick it.
  • Health, veterinary, restaurant, home-services and auto-repair agents follow extra safety rules your own instructions cannot remove.
  • Call audio is now only saved if you turn on “Save call audio”. Transcripts and summaries are unchanged.

1.10.0

  • New: live chat with your team. Connect your team’s Telegram group under Voice AI → Staff Requests. When a chat visitor asks for a person, the group gets their request and the conversation so far, and whoever taps “I’ll take it” chats with them from Telegram while they stay on your site. The visitor sees how long they may wait.
  • If nobody takes it in the time you set, the request is saved and the visitor is told your team will get back to them, with a reference.
  • New: Staff Requests. What only a person can decide is recorded for your team to take, note and close, and visitors are told exactly the wording you choose. They can later ask where a request stands, with its reference and the email or phone they gave.
  • Replies to visitors are never sent from an administrator’s email address.

1.9.7

  • Security fix: despite what the 1.8.0 notes said, an order number alone, with no email, returned that order’s status, items and total. The email is now always required, and a wrong email gets the same reply as an order that does not exist.
  • Failed order lookups pause for an hour after five misses, only for the conversation, order number or email being guessed at, never for your whole store.
  • Fixed: a voice call ended by silence no longer reads “Call ended by assistant” and closes the panel.

1.9.6

  • The voice tab now tells visitors that their call is recorded and transcribed, in their own language, before they press Start. Some places require everyone in a conversation to be told before recording begins. If you disclose it elsewhere on your site, turn it off under Voice AI → Widget → Privacy.
  • WordPress’s own privacy tools now cover the plugin. An export or erase request for a visitor’s email address includes the contact details they gave the assistant, and the Privacy Policy Guide in Settings → Privacy offers suggested wording you can adopt.
  • Call recordings are now deleted after 30 days and transcripts after 90 days, with the short AI summary kept so older sessions still show what they were about. The External Services section of this readme previously said visitor audio was only processed for the length of the call; it now describes what is actually stored, and for how long.

On the Premium and Enterprise plans, voice conversations are powered by OpenAI’s Realtime API instead. The plugin does not contact OpenAI directly — all requests go through api2.studiometa.io, which forwards them to OpenAI. You do not need an OpenAI account or API key. Plans other than Premium and Enterprise do not use this service.

Data sent: the visitor’s microphone audio and typed messages during a voice conversation, plus your configured agent name, greeting, system prompt and knowledge base.

  • OpenAI Terms of Use: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use
  • OpenAI Privacy Policy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy

6. Google Calendar (calendar.googleapis.com) — optional, only if you connect it

What it does: Lets the AI agent book real appointments during a conversation. Reads busy times from your connected Google Calendar so the agent never offers a slot you’re already booked, and creates a calendar event when a visitor books.

When it is contacted: Only if you explicitly connect Google Calendar under Voice AI → Appointments by clicking “Connect Google Calendar” and signing in through Google’s own consent screen. If you never connect it, the plugin never contacts Google Calendar, and appointment booking still works from the working hours you set — it simply won’t check your calendar for conflicts.

  • When you connect: a one-time OAuth sign-in with Google, requesting only free/busy visibility and the ability to create/edit events it creates — never your full calendar or any other Google data
  • When a visitor asks about availability: your calendar’s busy times are checked (cached briefly) to avoid offering a taken slot
  • When a visitor books: an event is created on your calendar with the appointment details

Data sent: an encrypted access credential (stored on StudioMeta’s servers, never in your WordPress database), and appointment details (visitor name, email, and time) when creating a calendar event.

Data NOT sent: the content of your other calendar events, contacts, or any other Google account data.

You can disconnect at any time from Voice AI → Appointments, or by revoking access directly from your Google Account permissions page.

  • Google Calendar Terms: https://developers.google.com/terms
  • Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

7. Twilio (api.twilio.com) — optional, only if you connect it

What it does: Lets real phone calls to a phone number you own be answered by your AI agent, using your own Twilio account. You keep your own Twilio account, buy your own number, and pay Twilio directly for call minutes and number rental — StudioMeta does not resell or bill you for Twilio usage. Talk time on answered calls counts against the same monthly voice minutes as the website widget.

When it is contacted: Only if you explicitly connect a Twilio account under Voice AI → Integrations by entering your Twilio Account SID, Auth Token, and phone number. If you never connect it, the plugin never contacts Twilio.

  • When you connect: your Account SID and Auth Token are verified once against Twilio to confirm they are valid before being saved
  • When someone calls your connected number: Twilio sends the call to StudioMeta’s servers, and the caller’s audio and the agent’s replies are streamed for the duration of the call

Data sent: your Twilio Account SID and Auth Token (stored encrypted on StudioMeta’s servers, never in your WordPress database), the phone number you connected, and during calls: the caller’s audio. Phone calls are transcribed on our servers exactly as widget calls are, and recorded only if you turn on Save call audio, with the same 30-day retention for the audio.

Data NOT sent: your Twilio billing details, SMS messages, call recordings held in your Twilio account, or any other data from your Twilio account.

You can disconnect at any time from Voice AI → Integrations, or by removing the webhook from your number in the Twilio Console.

  • Twilio Terms of Service: https://www.twilio.com/legal/tos
  • Twilio Privacy Policy: https://www.twilio.com/legal/privacy

8. Telegram (indirectly, via api2.studiometa.io) — optional, only if you connect a group

Lets your team take over a chat from your own Telegram group, connected under Voice AI → Staff Requests. The plugin never contacts Telegram itself; StudioMeta’s servers relay messages. When a chat visitor asks for a person, the group receives their request, the contact details they gave and the conversation so far, then the messages exchanged while a team member chats with them. Those messages stay in your group, under Telegram’s terms, until you delete them. Without a connected group nothing is sent to Telegram.

  • Telegram Terms of Service: https://telegram.org/tos
  • Telegram Privacy Policy: https://telegram.org/privacy

How to opt out

If you do not want the plugin to contact these services, simply deactivate and uninstall the plugin. The plugin cannot function without the hosted services because the AI assistant runs on our infrastructure (similar to how an Akismet plugin needs the Akismet service, or a Mailchimp plugin needs Mailchimp).

Third-Party Assets

Vazirmatn v33.003 by Saber Rastikerdar, used for Persian and Arabic text.
Licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (see assets/fonts/OFL.txt) and
distributed unmodified. Only the Non-Latin subset is bundled, and it is served
from this plugin folder — no font CDN is contacted, so no visitor or
administrator IP address is sent to a third party.
Source: https://github.com/rastikerdar/vazirmatn

upgrade_notice.1.11.0: Adds a guided setup on the dashboard. A site that has not chosen a business type sees it once; close it with Not now. Nothing in an existing setup changes unless you go through it.
upgrade_notice.1.10.1: Call audio is no longer saved unless you turn on "Save call audio" under Voice AI → Widget. Pick your business type from the setup steps on the dashboard.
upgrade_notice.1.10.0: Adds live chat with your team through your own Telegram group, and Staff Requests for what only a person can decide. Both are off until you set them up.
upgrade_notice.1.9.7: Security fix: the WooCommerce order lookup now always requires the email the order was placed with, and limits repeated failed attempts. Update now if the Store Assistant is enabled.
upgrade_notice.1.9.6: Tells visitors that their voice call is recorded before it starts, and adds support for WordPress's personal-data export and erase tools. Recommended for all users.
upgrade_notice.1.9.5: Adds Smart Navigation — the assistant can take a visitor to the page that answers them — and keeps a conversation going as they move around your site. Nothing opens any page until you list them yourself.
upgrade_notice.1.8.0: Adds the WooCommerce Store Assistant: the agent answers order and product questions from your store, including order status for guest checkouts, and can hand a visitor a link that fills their cart. Off until you enable it; nothing changes without WooCommerce.
upgrade_notice.1.7.23: Fixes admin notices that could not be permanently dismissed outside the plugin's own pages — closing one only hid it until the next page load. Recommended for all users.
upgrade_notice.1.7.22: Fixes a connected HubSpot account collecting duplicate, half-empty contacts for a single visitor. Recommended if you use the HubSpot integration.
upgrade_notice.1.7.21: Privacy and performance release. Uninstalling now removes all stored data including captured leads, the widget script no longer blocks page rendering, and the assistant is more usable with a screen reader. Recommended for all users.
upgrade_notice.1.7.20: Security release. The widget no longer places long-lived credentials in your page HTML — it now requests a short-lived, single-site token when a conversation starts. Recommended for all users.
upgrade_notice.1.7.19: Fixes a phone number sometimes displaying with the "+" in the wrong place in a right-to-left conversation (Persian, Arabic). Cosmetic only — recommended for anyone using a right-to-left language.
upgrade_notice.1.7.18: Fixes the assistant occasionally inventing a phone number when asked how to reach you. Recommended for all users. After upgrading, set your number in Settings → Business Phone, or leave it empty if you have none.
upgrade_notice.1.2.0: Per-site agent isolation. If you have used the same license on multiple sites, please review your active site after upgrade.
upgrade_notice.1.1.1: Critical fix: text fields no longer accumulate backslashes on save. Recommended for all users.
upgrade_notice.1.1.0: Adds free trial, smart quota fallback, and auto-upgrade. Recommended for all users.
